title: A complete-intersection local ring has a principal global-complete-intersection neighbourhood
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $F$ be a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $Q\subset F$ be a prime ideal [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose that $F_Q$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$: there exist a regular local $k$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] and a finite regular sequence $a_1,\ldots,a_c$ in its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] such that $F_Q\cong A/(a_1,\ldots,a_c)$ as $k$-algebras. Then there exists $h\in F\setminus Q$ such that $F_h=F[1/h]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].

source.place: Tag 00SG (lemma-lci-at-prime), implication (1) => (3), lines 36159–36180; local-ring meaning is Definition Tag 00SD (definition-lci-local-ring), lines 36013–36028.

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation $\pi:P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow F$ (possible because $F$ is a finite type $k$-algebra), put $I=\ker(\pi)$, and let $\mathfrak q' = \pi^{-1}(Q)$. The induced map $P_{\mathfrak q'}\to F_Q$ is a surjective local $k$-algebra map, and the localization-at-a-quotient identification gives $F_Q\cong P_{\mathfrak q'}/IP_{\mathfrak q'}$. Thus its kernel is exactly $IP_{\mathfrak q'}$.

source.place: Tag 00SG, proof of (1) => (3), using the chosen polynomial presentation and the localization of a quotient.

proof.text: The ring $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a regular local $k$-algebra: the polynomial-ring regularity statement gives that every localization of $P$ at a prime is regular local. It is essentially of finite type over $k$ because it is a localization of the finite type algebra $P$; the localization map $P_{\mathfrak q'}\to F_Q$ is local because it is the quotient map to the local ring $P_{\mathfrak q'}/IP_{\mathfrak q'}$.

source.place: Tag 00SG, proof of (1) => (3), with polynomial-ring regularity from Tag 00OQ.

proof.text: The assumed isomorphism $F_Q\cong A/(a_1,\dots,a_c)$ transports the quotient map from the regular local ring $A$ to a surjective local $k$-algebra map $A\twoheadrightarrow F_Q$. Its kernel is generated by the given finite regular sequence $a_1,\dots,a_c$ contained in the maximal ideal of $A$. Applying the regular-sequence-kernel invariance lemma to the two surjective local maps $P_{\mathfrak q'}\twoheadrightarrow F_Q$ and $A\twoheadrightarrow F_Q$ shows that $IP_{\mathfrak q'}$ is generated by a finite regular sequence in the maximal ideal of $P_{\mathfrak q'}$.

source.place: Tag 00SF, equivalence of conditions (1) and (2), with the local-ring definition in Tag 00SD.

proof.text: Apply the principal-neighbourhood complete-intersection lemma to the polynomial presentation $F=P/I$, the prime $Q$, and the regular sequence generating $IP_{\mathfrak q'}$. It yields an element $h\in F\setminus Q$ such that $F_h=F[1/h]$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.
